title_en: A scholar’s life-entry and a classical letter
q_en: How do I read a scholar’s biography entry, and the opening and closing of a classical letter?
q_ar: كَيْفَ أَقْرَأُ تَرْجَمَةَ عَالِمٍ وَبِدَايَةَ الرِّسَالَةِ وَنِهَايَتَهَا؟
not_yet: Long biographical entries with their lists of books: not yet.
The many types of the letters of the tradition (a fatwā, a will): Lesson 85.
Telling the sender’s titles apart from his name in long openings: it comes with practice.
not_yet_ar: التَّرَاجِمُ الطَّوِيلَةُ وَقَوَائِمُ الْمُؤَلَّفَاتِ: لَيْسَ الْآنَ.
التَّمْيِيزُ بَيْنَ أَلْقَابِ الْكَاتِبِ وَاسْمِهِ فِي الِافْتِتَاحِ الطَّوِيلِ: يَأْتِي بِالْمُمَارَسَةِ.

slides.head_en: Look: the entry of a scholar
sents: Shaykh Sālim was born in Tarim.
He read with his shaykh in jurisprudence.
Then he travelled to Mecca and made the pilgrimage.
He died in Tarim and was buried there.
legend: Verb: one event of his life

slides.head_en: Look: the frame of a letter
sents: And now: peace be upon you.
And do not forget us in your prayers.

lines: In the entry, which verbs give birth, study, death and burial? Which of them name no doer?
فِي التَّرْجَمَةِ: أَيُّ الْأَفْعَالِ لِلْمَوْلِدِ وَالدِّرَاسَةِ وَالْوَفَاةِ وَالدَّفْنِ؟ وَأَيُّهَا بِلَا فَاعِلٍ؟
In the letter, which little word marks who writes, and which marks who receives?
فِي الرِّسَالَةِ: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ لِلْكَاتِبِ وَأَيُّهَا لِلْمُرْسَلِ إِلَيْهِ؟
Which word turns the letter from its address to its greeting and business? Which word ends it?
أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَنْقُلُ الرِّسَالَةَ مِنَ الْعُنْوَانِ إِلَى التَّحِيَّةِ وَالْمَوْضُوعِ؟ وَأَيُّهَا تُنْهِيهَا؟

slides.head_en: Two texts with a fixed frame

cards.def_en: Past verbs in the order of a life.
مِنْ: who writes. إِلَى: who receives.

cards.def_ar: تَأْتِي بَعْدَ «مِنْ … إِلَى …» وَتَقُودُ إِلَى التَّحِيَّةِ وَالْمَوْضُوعِ.
cards.def_en: It comes after “from … to …” and leads into the greeting and the business.
The last word of the letter.

slides.tip: In a letter مِنْ and إِلَى decide who is who. In an entry, عَلَى after قَرَأَ means “with a teacher”.
slides.tip_ar: فِي الرِّسَالَةِ «مِنْ» وَ«إِلَى» تُحَدِّدَانِ الْكَاتِبَ وَالْمُرْسَلَ إِلَيْهِ. وَفِي التَّرْجَمَةِ «قَرَأَ عَلَى» تَعْنِي عِنْدَ شَيْخٍ.

slides.head_en: How to read an entry and a letter
lines: Entry: follow the verbs in order: وُلِدَ، قَرَأَ، سَافَرَ، تُوُفِّيَ، دُفِنَ.
Entry: a long line of names is one person: بْنُ means “son of”.
فِي التَّرْجَمَةِ: سِلْسِلَةُ الْأَسْمَاءِ شَخْصٌ وَاحِدٌ، وَ«بْنُ» تَعْنِي «ابْنُ».
Letter: first find مِنْ and إِلَى, then وَبَعْدُ.
Letter: the end is a request for prayer and then وَالسَّلَامُ.

items: letter: the hinge and the greeting

slides.why: A student reads this as “to Ahmad, from his father”. Wrong! مِنْ marks the one who writes and إِلَى the one who receives: it is from Ahmad to his father.
slides.why_ar: قَرَأَ طَالِبٌ: «إِلَى أَحْمَدَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ». خَطَأٌ! «مِنْ» لِلْكَاتِبِ وَ«إِلَى» لِلْمُرْسَلِ إِلَيْهِ: الرِّسَالَةُ مِنْ أَحْمَدَ إِلَى أَبِيهِ.

slides.head_en: From Khulāṣat al-Athar: the entry of a scholar
lines: وُلِدَ بِتَرِيمَ فِي سَنَةِ تِسْعِينَ وَتِسْعِمِائَةٍ وَحَفِظَ الْقُرْآنَ عَلَى الْمُعَلِّمِ الْأَدِيبِ عُمَرَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللهِ الْخَطِيبِ
He was born in Tarīm in the year 990 and memorised the Qurʾān with the cultured teacher ʿUmar b. ʿAbdallāh al-Khaṭīb.
وَرَبَّاهُ وَالِدُهُ وَأَدَّبَهُ مُعَلِّمُهُ بِأَحْسَنِ تَرْبِيَةٍ وَمَاتَ أَبُوهُ وَهُوَ دُونَ الِاحْتِلَامِ
His father brought him up and his teacher trained him in the best way; his father died while he was under the age of puberty,
slides.source: Khulāṣat al-Athar of al-Muḥibbī (the entry of Abū Bakr b. Aḥmad al-Shillī Bāʿalawī)

slides.head_en: From Mukātabāt al-Imām al-Ḥaddād: the address of a letter
slides.head_ar: مِنْ مُكَاتَبَاتِ الْإِمَامِ الْحَدَّادِ: عُنْوَانُ رِسَالَةٍ
lines: عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَلَوِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ الْحَدَّادِ عَلَوِيِّ، إِلَى حَضْرَةِ الْأَخِ الْوَفِيِّ، السَّيِّدِ الصَّفِيِّ، وَالْعَارِفِ الصُّوفِيِّ
ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī b. Muḥammad al-Ḥaddād ʿAlawī, to the presence of the loyal brother, the pure sayyid, the Sufi knower,
الشَّيْخِ الْحَبِيبِ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ السَّيِّدِ شَيْخِ السَّقَّافِ بَاعَلَوِي، نَفَعَ اللهُ بِهِ وَبِسَلَفِهِ الصَّالِحِ فِي الدَّارَيْنِ، آمِينَ
the shaykh and beloved Abū Bakr b. al-Sayyid Shaykh al-Saqqāf Bāʿalawī: may God benefit through him and his righteous forebears in both abodes, amen.

can: I can read a scholar’s entry and say when and where he was born, with whom he studied, and where he died and was buried.
I can find who writes to whom in a classical letter, and its greeting, its hinge وَبَعْدُ and its ending.
I can tell an entry, a letter and the other text types of this level apart.
can_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ تَرْجَمَةَ عَالِمٍ وَأَقُولَ مَتَى وَأَيْنَ وُلِدَ، وَعِنْدَ مَنْ دَرَسَ، وَأَيْنَ تُوُفِّيَ وَدُفِنَ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَجِدَ مَنْ يَكْتُبُ إِلَى مَنْ فِي رِسَالَةٍ قَدِيمَةٍ، وَتَحِيَّتَهَا وَ«وَبَعْدُ» وَخَاتِمَتَهَا.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُمَيِّزَ التَّرْجَمَةَ وَالرِّسَالَةَ وَسَائِرَ أَنْوَاعِ النُّصُوصِ فِي هَذَا الْمُسْتَوَى.

sections.name: A
sections.en: From the entry of a scholar. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: فَقَامَ بِتَرْبِيَتِهِ شَيْخُهُ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ شِهَابِ الدِّينِ
and his teacher, the Shaykh of Islam ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Shihāb al-Dīn, undertook his upbringing.
ثُمَّ اشْتَغَلَ بِتَحْصِيلِ الْعُلُومِ الشَّرْعِيَّةِ فَقَرَأَ الْفِقْهَ عَلَى شَيْخِهِ الْمَذْكُورِ
Then he busied himself acquiring the religious sciences, and read jurisprudence with the teacher just mentioned,
وَقَرَأَ عَلَيْهِ فِي الْحَدِيثِ وَالتَّفْسِيرِ وَالتَّصَوُّفِ وَالْعَرَبِيَّةِ
and read with him in ḥadīth, Qurʾān commentary, Sufism and Arabic.
sections.source: Khulāṣat al-Athar of al-Muḥibbī (the entry of Abū Bakr b. Aḥmad al-Shillī Bāʿalawī)
sections.cite: Tarjama: Muḥammad Amīn al-Muḥibbī, Khulāṣat al-athar fī aʿyān al-qarn al-ḥādī ʿashar (d. 1111 AH), the entry of al-sayyid Abū Bakr b. Aḥmad al-Shillī Bāʿalawī, which quotes his son Muḥammad al-Shillī's al-Mashraʿ al-Rawī; Shamela Master Library copy (Bafaqih 22222 install, id 48410, 1978 pp; the same work is Shamela 3.28 id 7146), copy pages 71–72 (its own counter; printed edition not identified). Letters: ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, Mukātabāt al-Imām al-Ḥaddād, part 1 ("Jāmiʿ al-mukātabāt wa-l-waṣāyā wa-l-kalimāt wa-l-qaṣāʾid"), a printed edition (publisher and year not identified from the scan; TLNOOR id 144, OCR PDF), printed p. 43 (lines 7–10: the opening of the first letter) and p. 92 (lines 11–14: the end of a later letter); read against the page images. Abridged: lines 3–5 of the tarjama (the research file has 14 lines); the copy is unvowelled and the vowels are added by the course (vowelled for learners).
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them. The entry itself is one long run of past verbs; help the class see each verb as one event of the scholar’s life.

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
items.model: and his teacher, the Shaykh of Islam ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Shihāb al-Dīn, undertook his upbringing.

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
items.model: Then he busied himself acquiring the religious sciences, and read jurisprudence with the teacher just mentioned,

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
items.model: and read with him in ḥadīth, Qur’ān commentary, Sufism and Arabic.

items.en: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
items.model: A biography entry (tarjama) of a scholar, from Khulāṣat al-Athar of al-Muḥibbī.

items.ar_q: مَنْ قَامَ بِتَرْبِيَتِهِ؟
items.model: His teacher, the Shaykh of Islam ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Shihāb al-Dīn.

items.en: Which sciences did he read with that teacher? (line 3)
items.ar_q: أَيَّ الْعُلُومِ قَرَأَ عَلَيْهِ؟
options: Ḥadīth, Qur’ān commentary (tafsīr), Sufism and Arabic.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Shihāb al-Dīn, named in line 1.
items.answer: Ḥadīth, Qur’ān commentary (tafsīr), Sufism and Arabic.
items.model: Ḥadīth, Qur’ān commentary (tafsīr), Sufism and Arabic. (Jurisprudence, in line 2.)

items.en: What does ثُمَّ show at the start of line 2?
items.ar_q: عَلَى مَاذَا تَدُلُّ «ثُمَّ» فِي بِدَايَةِ السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟
items.model: The next stage of his life: after his upbringing, his studies.

items.en: Which little word comes after قَرَأَ and means “with (a teacher)”?
items.ar_q: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ بَعْدَ «قَرَأَ» يَعْنِي «عِنْدَ شَيْخٍ»؟
options: Ḥadīth, Qur’ān commentary (tafsīr), Sufism and Arabic.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Shihāb al-Dīn, named in line 1.
items.model: عَلَى.

items.ar_q: مَنْ «شَيْخُهُ الْمَذْكُورُ»؟
options: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Shihāb al-Dīn, named in line 1.
Ḥadīth, Qur’ān commentary (tafsīr), Sufism and Arabic.
items.answer: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Shihāb al-Dīn, named in line 1.
items.model: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Shihāb al-Dīn, named in line 1.

items.en: ★ What does بْنُ mean here? How many names make up the teacher’s name?
items.ar_q: ★ مَا مَعْنَى «بْنُ» هُنَا؟ كَمْ شَخْصًا فِي الِاسْمِ؟
items.model: بْنُ = “son of”. The name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, son of Shihāb al-Dīn: one person, with a title (شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ) before it.

items.en: ★ Why does line 2 write “his teacher just mentioned” and not the name again?
items.ar_q: ★ لِمَاذَا لَمْ يُكَرِّرِ الْكَاتِبُ الِاسْمَ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟
items.model: The entry has already named him in line 1; a biography avoids repeating a name that is clear.

sections.name: B
sections.en: From the letters of Imam al-Ḥaddād. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: وَبَعْدُ، فَالسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، وَمَغْفِرَتُهُ وَرِضْوَانُهُ، وَقَدْ وَصَلَ إِلَيْنَا
And then: peace be upon you, and God's mercy, blessings, forgiveness and good pleasure; and there has reached us...
وَقَدْ وَصَلَتْ مِنْكُمْ حَفِظَكُمُ اللهُ إِلَيْنَا كُتُبٌ عَدِيدَةٌ، وَكُلُّهَا حَسَنَةٌ مُفِيدَةٌ
(Letter, closing, from a later letter in the same book:) Many letters from you, God keep you, have reached us, all of them good and useful.
وَلَا تَنْسَوْنَا أَنْتُمْ مِنْ صَالِحِ دُعَائِكُمْ
And do not forget us in your good prayers.
sections.source: Mukātabāt al-Imām al-Ḥaddād (the greeting of a letter, and the end of another)

items.en: Translate line 1 (it stops where the source goes on).
items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
items.model: And now: peace be upon you, and God’s mercy, blessings, forgiveness and good pleasure; and there has reached us…

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
items.model: Many letters from you, God keep you, have reached us, all of them good and useful.

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَيْنِ الثَّالِثَ وَالرَّابِعَ.
options: Four: mercy, blessings, forgiveness, good pleasure.
And do not forget us in your good prayers. And peace.
Not to forget him in his good prayers: a request for du‘ā’.
items.answer: And do not forget us in your good prayers. And peace.
items.model: And do not forget us in your good prayers. And peace.

items.en: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
items.model: A classical letter (the greeting and the end), from Mukātabāt al-Imām al-Ḥaddād.

items.en: What does وَبَعْدُ do in a letter?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ «وَبَعْدُ» فِي الرِّسَالَةِ؟
items.model: It is the hinge: it follows the address (from … to …) and leads into the greeting and the letter’s message.

items.en: How many blessings are named after “peace” in line 1? Which?
items.ar_q: كَمْ دُعَاءً بَعْدَ «السَّلَامِ» فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ؟ مَا هِيَ؟
options: And do not forget us in your good prayers. And peace.
Four: mercy, blessings, forgiveness, good pleasure.
Not to forget him in his good prayers: a request for du‘ā’.
items.answer: Four: mercy, blessings, forgiveness, good pleasure.
items.model: Four: mercy, blessings, forgiveness, good pleasure.

items.en: What is this little phrase inside line 2, and who is it said to?
items.ar_q: مَا هَذِهِ الْعِبَارَةُ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟ وَلِمَنْ تُقَالُ؟
items.model: “God keep you”: a short prayer for the receiver, said to him by the writer.

items.ar: وَلَا تَنْسَوْنَا أَنْتُمْ مِنْ صَالِحِ دُعَائِكُمْ
items.en: What does the writer ask of the receiver in line 3?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا يَطْلُبُ الْكَاتِبُ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ؟
options: Not to forget him in his good prayers: a request for du‘ā’.
Four: mercy, blessings, forgiveness, good pleasure.
And do not forget us in your good prayers. And peace.
items.answer: Not to forget him in his good prayers: a request for du‘ā’.
items.model: Not to forget him in his good prayers: a request for du‘ā’.

items.ar_q: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تُنْهِي الرِّسَالَةَ؟
options: Not to forget him in his good prayers: a request for du‘ā’.
And do not forget us in your good prayers. And peace.
Four: mercy, blessings, forgiveness, good pleasure.
items.model: وَالسَّلَامُ: “and peace”.

items.en: ★ The letter is to one man, yet it says عَلَيْكُمْ (“you all”). Why?
items.ar_q: ★ الرِّسَالَةُ إِلَى رَجُلٍ وَاحِدٍ لَكِنَّهَا تَقُولُ «عَلَيْكُمْ». لِمَاذَا؟
items.model: The plural of respect: a writer honours the one he writes to by using “you” in the plural.

items.en: ★ Line 2 says the letters were “good and useful”. What do the writer’s words tell you about how the two men wrote to each other?
items.ar_q: ★ مَاذَا تُخْبِرُنَا كَلِمَاتُ السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي عَنْ مُكَاتَبَةِ الرَّجُلَيْنِ؟
items.model: They wrote often: many letters had arrived, and the writer valued them.

sections.name: C
sections.en: A short text: a letter from Ahmad to his father. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: مِنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ إِلَى أَبِيهِ الْكَرِيمِ.
From Ahmad b. ʿAlī to his noble father.

sections.name: AA
sections.en: The Story Strip: lines 1–153
lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.
The Habib sat in the mosque.
The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
The boy came in through the door.
The mother looked at the boy.
The boy sits in the study circle today.
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
The boy was happy in the majlis.
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.
The boy helped the guests and honoured them.
The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
The boy was humble and learned from them.
اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.
اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.
حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.
أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.
The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.
The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.
مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening.
The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is!
قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ.
The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm.
And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ.
The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.
The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word.
ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْجَذْرَ وَالْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ مَتْنًا صَغِيرًا.
The boy read a small matn (a short base text) with the Habib.
أَصْبَحَ الْمَتْنُ سَهْلًا لَكِنَّ الدَّرْسَ طَوِيلٌ.
The matn became easy, but the lesson is long.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ مُسْرِعًا وَجَلَسَ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ.
The boy came to the lesson hurrying, and sat facing the qibla.
And the Habib was pleased with him.
ذَكَرَ الْوَلَدُ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَصَلَّى عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ ثَلَاثًا.
The boy remembered Allah a great deal and prayed for blessings on the Prophet ﷺ three times.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ مَرَّتَيْنِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
The boy read the lesson twice, seeking knowledge.
The Habib gave the boy a small book.
ظَنَّ الْوَلَدُ الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا فَقَالَ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ.
The boy thought the book difficult, so he said: There is no power and no strength except through Allah.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ أَرْكَانَ الْوُضُوءِ: الْأَوَّلُ النِّيَّةُ، وَالثَّانِي غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ.
The boy wrote the pillars of the ablution: the first, the intention; and the second, washing the face.
وَالثَّالِثُ غَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ، وَالرَّابِعُ مَسْحُ بَعْضِ الرَّأْسِ.
And the third, washing the hands; and the fourth, wiping part of the head.
The boy read the wird in the morning.
ثُمَّ دَعَا: يَا رَبِّ، اِهْدِنَا وَاعْفُ عَنَّا، آمِينَ.
Then he made duʿāʾ: O my Lord, guide us and pardon us. Amen.
شَرِبَ الْوَلَدُ مِنْ مَاءِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمَا شَرِبَ إِلَّا مَاءً طَاهِرًا.
The boy drank from the water of the mosque, and he drank only pure water.
Neither its colour nor its taste had changed.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ اِسْمَ الشَّيْخِ عَلَى الْكِتَابِ: سَالِمُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ.
The boy read the shaykh’s name on the book: Salim son of Yusuf.
And his kunya is Abū Aḥmad.
رَغِبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْأَجْرِ وَرَغِبَ عَنِ الْإِثْمِ.
The boy desired knowledge and reward, and turned away from sin.
فَقَالَ لَهُ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا تَرْغَبْ فِي الدُّنْيَا.
So the Habib said to him: Do not set your desire on this world.
اِسْتَيْقَظَ الْوَلَدُ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ وَأَخَذَ السِّوَاكَ.
The boy woke up before dawn and took the siwāk.
Then he sat and strove in his wird.
The boy never missed the rawḥa.
يَحْضُرُ الْوَلَدُ الرَّوْحَةَ دَائِمًا وَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ جِدًّا.
The boy always attends the rawḥa, and he is very happy.
A letter arrived from the boy’s uncle.
بَدَأَ الْعَمُّ رِسَالَتَهُ: أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَاطْلُبِ الْعِلْمَ.
The uncle began his letter: Now then, seek knowledge.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ لِأُمِّهِ: هَذَا هُوَ الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy said to his mother: This is the book that I read with the Habib.
It is a small book that I read three times.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ لِيَحْضُرَ الدَّرْسَ.
The boy went to the mosque to attend the lesson.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِيَتَعَلَّمْ كُلُّ طَالِبٍ كَيْ يَعْمَلَ بِعِلْمِهِ.
The Habib said: Let every student learn, so that he may act on his knowledge.
The Habib said: Whoever serves, learns.
وَإِذَا جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ فَهِمَ الدَّرْسَ.
And when the boy sat in the majlis, he understood the lesson.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ: وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ فِي صَفَرَ سَنَةَ أَلْفٍ وَأَرْبَعٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ.
The boy wrote: The Imam was born in Ṣafar, in the year one thousand and forty-four.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ آيَةً ثُمَّ قَرَأَ تَفْسِيرَهَا.
The Habib read a verse, then read its commentary.
ثُمَّ قَالَ: الْحِكْمَةُ، أَيِ الْعِلْمُ وَالْعَمَلُ.
Then he said: Wisdom, that is, knowledge and action.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ الْإِسْنَادَ ثُمَّ الْمَتْنَ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ.
The Habib read the chain, then the matn: The Prophet ﷺ said: Religion is sincere counsel.
وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَعْنَى الْحَدِيثِ: عِمَادُ الدِّينِ النَّصِيحَةُ.
And the Habib said: The meaning of the ḥadīth: the pillar of religion is sincere counsel.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ.
The boy heard in the majlis: The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever guides to good has a reward like that of the one who does it.
ثُمَّ دَلَّ الْوَلَدُ صَدِيقَهُ عَلَى الْمَجْلِسِ.
Then the boy guided his friend to the majlis.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الرَّوْحَةِ مِنَ الْمَتْنِ: يُسَنُّ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ فِي أَرْبَعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ.
In the rawḥa the Habib read from the matn: Raising the hands is recommended in four places.
ثُمَّ سَأَلَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَا حُكْمُ رَفْعِ الْيَدَيْنِ؟ فَقَالَ الْوَلَدُ: سُنَّةٌ.
Then the Habib asked: What is the ruling on raising the hands? The boy said: A sunna.
قَرَأَتْ مَرْيَمُ عَقِيدَةً صَغِيرَةً فِي الْبَيْتِ وَسَمِعَهَا الْوَلَدُ.
Maryam read a small creed at home, and the boy listened to her.
She said: Allah exists; He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
قَالَ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ: يَا بُنَيَّ، عَلَيْكَ بِأَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فِيهَا.
The boy’s father said: My son, hold fast to returning what is entrusted, and beware of betraying it.
And hold fast to truthful speech and to keeping a promise.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ نَصِيحَةً طَوِيلَةً عَنِ التَّقْوَى.
The Habib read a long counsel about taqwā (God-consciousness).
وَمَعْنَاهَا: مَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ عَاجِلٍ وَلَا آجِلٍ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى سَبِيلٌ إِلَيْهِ.
And its meaning: There is no good, present or future, but taqwā is a road to it.
قَرَأَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ الرَّاتِبَ بَعْدَ الْعِشَاءِ وَحَضَرَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَهُمْ.
The people of Tarim read the Rātib after ʿIshāʾ, and the boy attended with them.
وَقَالُوا: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ثَلَاثًا.
And they said: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created (three times).
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْمَوْلِدِ اِجْتَمَعَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
On the night of the mawlid the people of Tarim gathered in the mosque.
وَقَرَأَ الْجَمِيعُ الْمَوْلِدَ وَذَكَرُوا جَمَالَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَكَمَالَهُ.
And everyone read the mawlid and they mentioned the beauty of the Prophet ﷺ and his perfection.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ قَصِيدَةً فِي مَدْحِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.
The boy heard in the majlis a qaṣīda in praise of the Prophet ﷺ.
And in every verse there is a first half and a second half.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ سِيرَةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ: وُلِدَ فِي مَكَّةَ وَنَشَأَ يَتِيمًا وَكَفَلَهُ جَدُّهُ.
The boy read the life of the Prophet ﷺ: He was born in Mecca, grew up an orphan, and his grandfather took him in his care.
So the boy loved the Prophet ﷺ even more.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ رِسَالَةً مِنْ رَسَائِلِ الْإِمَامِ.
The boy copied out a letter from the letters of the Imam.
وَكَانَ فِي أَوَّلِهَا: وَبَعْدُ، وَفِي آخِرِهَا: وَالسَّلَامُ.
At its beginning was: “And now”, and at its end: “And peace”.
